title: T1608.001 — Stage Capabilities - Upload Malware
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Stage Capabilities - Upload Malware with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated diagram: an attacker builds an infostealer, uploads it to a free file host, builds a decoy page, shares the link, and an employee downloads and runs it while the SOC watches proxy, mail and EDR telemetry.

nodes.label: Attacker
nodes.tip: The threat actor. Builds the payload and drives the whole staging flow.

nodes.label: File host
nodes.tip: A consumer file-hosting service. It holds the archive and hands out short share links.

nodes.label: Decoy page
nodes.tip: A harmless-looking page that makes the download feel like a business document.

nodes.label: Employee
nodes.tip: An office worker. Their download is the moment staging becomes a real compromise.

nodes.label: SOC analyst
nodes.tip: The defender. Joins feeds, proxy, and EDR signals to catch the staged file.

steps.title: Build the payload
steps.caption: The attacker finalizes an infostealer build and checks it against security tools in a private sandbox. Nothing is public yet.
steps.defender: No telemetry yet - the test run happens entirely on the attacker's side.

detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Create an anonymous account
steps.caption: A throwaway email address registers a free account on a one-click file host. The whole step takes two minutes.
steps.defender: Nothing visible. The account exists only on the provider's side.

steps.title: Upload and get a link
steps.caption: The installer archive is uploaded. The host returns a short share link that works from any browser.
steps.defender: Within hours, malware databases record the file hash as first-seen - the earliest outside signal.

steps.title: Build the decoy page
steps.caption: A fake invoice-viewer page is published so the download feels like an ordinary business document.
steps.defender: URL scanning services may fingerprint the page if a crawler stumbles on it before the campaign starts.

steps.title: Send the link
steps.caption: The share link goes out in one short email and one forum post. The lure promises a document the victim expects.
steps.defender: The mail gateway rewrites and tracks the URL but has no reputation data to judge the host - your visibility starts here.

steps.title: Victim downloads
steps.caption: The employee clicks through the decoy and the browser saves the archive to the Downloads folder.
steps.defender: First internal evidence: a proxy line for an archive from a rare host, plus an EDR file event with the internet-zone marker.

fields.detail: The employee clicks through the decoy and the browser saves the archive to the Downloads folder.

detection.label: Partial signal
detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: Payload runs
steps.caption: The archive is opened and the stealer reads browser password stores and cookies, then sends a small POST with the loot.
steps.defender: EDR flags the script child process and credential-store access; the proxy sees a tiny POST to a never-seen panel.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: SOC responds
steps.caption: The analyst confirms the chain, blocks the file-host category, isolates the workstation, and rotates the user's credentials.
steps.defender: A 90-day hunt finds one more user who downloaded but never ran the file. The hash and host go to blocklists and the ISAC.
